category_title: Students who use physical presence and threats to intimidate faculty
minimal_context: The student arrives in the classroom during general instruction and confronts the professor in front of the other students.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Good morning everyone. Please take your seats so we can begin today's lecture.

STUDENT: (Slams textbook on the desk and refuses to return to his seat, standing in a power stance looking down to communicate dominance) I'm not sitting down.

TUTOR: I need you to go to your seat now.

STUDENT: (Uses a 'size up and down' nonverbal look at the professor) No.

TUTOR: We can discuss any issues after class. Let's move on.

STUDENT: (Yells out to the class) She is the worst teacher in the world! Don't pay attention to anything she says. She's stupid.

options.A: Provide a clear beginning and end for each instructional task during the lecture and throughout the general instruction period.
options.B: Add a section to the opening class defining communication expectations, and request that all questions be held until the end of the lecture to prevent students from taking over.
options.C: Guide the student to progressively and methodically tune their awareness to each body part, followed by intentionally relaxing each part from their toes to the top of their heads.
options.D: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation during the lecture, such as giving them a squishy, stress-relief ball.
